basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Erat autem terra labii unius et sermonum eorumdem. Quia praeoccupando dixerat filios Noe'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Erat autem terra labii unius et sermonum eorumdem. Quia praeoccupando dixerat filios Noe terram secundum cognationes et linguas et regiones in gentibus suis divisisse, redit ostendere quomodo fuerint homines ab invicem disjuncti: ubi certissime claret quia genus humanum quandiu Conditori suo debita humilitate servivit, etiam sibimetipsi pacifica charitate concordavit. At ubi contra Auctorem cervicem superbiens erexit, mox juste punitum, nec ad seipsum pacem habere potuit. Quanta autem hominum esse felicitas posset etiam paradiso dejectorum, si vel tunc Creatori suo servire humiliter vellent, testatur gratia ejusdem Domini Conditoris ac Redemptoris nostri, qui discipulis sibi fideliter adhaerentibus misso desuper Spiritu omnium notitiam tribuit linguarum; unde mira immutatione dexterae Excelsi factum est ut sicut hic linguis ob superbiam divisis gentes sunt ab invicem toto orbe dispersae, ita illic, ob meritum humilitatis, adunata diversitate linguarum, collecti ex omni natione quae sub coelo est populi una et non dispari confessione ac fide laudes et magnalia Dei resonarent; meritoque haec civitas, in qua linguae divisae ac gentes sunt dispersae, Babylon, id est Confusio; illa dicitur Jerusalem, id est, Visio pacis, in qua, adunatis in Dei laudem loquelis universarum gentium, est facta concordia. Sed haec postmodum latius. Interim textum litterae videamus
